subject: Post-demo: inference slate prioritization & ops path
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Kate Johnson <kate@axoncloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: inference slate prioritization & ops path

Hi Kate —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed prioritization so we can get a short, focused eval sprint running next week. I tried to keep this to the essentials so your engineering and procurement teams can see tradeoffs at a glance.

Snapshot: Axon use case = conversational support + grouped search over internal docs; target p95 latency < 350ms for short-turn chats; cost sensitivity for high-volume embedding/recall flows.

Recommended shortlist (ranked for first sprint):
1) open-vectra-7b-fp16 (Priority A)
   - Quality: high on instruction / chat / retrieval-augmented prompts (internal eval score: 89/100)
   - Median p95 latency (seq len ~256): ~180ms on one A10G equivalent GPU
   - Estimated cost: ~$0.85 / 1k tokens
   - When to pick: if quality is the main blocker and you can accept moderate infra cost

2) reed-13b-8bit (Priority B)
   - Quality: slightly better on longer form and complex reasoning (internal eval: 92/100)
   - Median p95 latency: ~320ms on a 40GB GPU with 8-bit kernels (expected higher memory footprint)
   - Estimated cost: ~$1.30 / 1k tokens (8bit optimized runtime)
   - When to pick: if you prioritize accuracy for escalation/summary flows and can tolerate higher cost

3) minigo-1.3b-quant (Priority C - low cost)
   - Quality: good for short Q&A/slot-filling (internal eval: 76/100)
   - Median p95 latency: ~90ms (very low)
   - Estimated cost: ~$0.22 / 1k tokens
   - When to pick: if throughput and cost are dominating and you accept lower breadth on reasoning

Why this slate? We balanced your p95 latency target, the retrieval-heavy profile, and a desire to avoid surprise quality regressions when moving to production. We also included a small, cheap option so you can route low-risk traffic (password resets, simple lookups) to the minigo model and reserve larger models for escalations.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- You: share 500–1k representative prompts (if possible) — we can run them against the shortlist and return per-prompt diffs. Attachment: axon_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample).
- Redwood: run an overnight batch test (latency + quality diff) and share the benchmark CSV and a short digest by EOD tomorrow. Attachment: benchmarks_initial_results.csv + Drive link below.
- Ops call: schedule a 45-minute technical sync (we suggest including your infra lead + procurement). Proposed slots attached in follow-up.

Quick notes on deployment options: hosted API is fastest to test; Dedicated capacity or Private (VPC) available for production if you need isolation + lower network egress latency. For Axon I recommend starting hosted for the eval and moving to Dedicated if you like the results.

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/axn/benchmarks/initial-results (benchmarks) | HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/AXON-12345

If this looks right, I’ll kick off the benchmark run once you confirm the prompt pack and availability for the ops call.

Thanks —
Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Avery — this is helpful. A few clarifying asks before you run the batch:

- Latency target: the 350ms p95 is for our US production region (short-turn chats only). For embeddings/recall we can tolerate higher latency but cost needs to be low. Can you include per-model embedding throughput (QPS) in the benchmark?
- Private deployment: we may need to run a pilot in our VPC for security reasons. Can the 7b fp16 option be run in Private/Dedicated and keep similar latency numbers?
- Audit logs: procurement is going to ask about auditability / data retention for the eval. Can you send the SOC2/Security doc or point me to the evidence pack?

We’ll also pull a 500-prompt subset from our transcripts and share before COB. If the results look good, procurement will ask for pricing for a 6-month commit and an initial 1-month trial environment.

—Kate
Kate Johnson
Head of Product, Axon Cloud

Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference slate prioritization & ops path

Kate — quick answers and an ops-oriented addendum so procurement/infra can see specifics.

1) Embedding throughput estimates (single 40GB GPU):
   - open-vectra-7b-fp16: ~220 QPS (batching to 128 vectors, deduped cache)
   - reed-13b-8bit: ~110 QPS (8-bit kernels are slower for dense embedding workloads)
   - minigo-1.3b-quant: ~650 QPS
   Note: these numbers are from the same benchmarking harness we used during the demo; we’ll surface per-batch histograms in the CSV.

2) Private/Dedicated viability:
   - open-vectra-7b-fp16: yes, fully supported on Redwood Private with near-parity latency when we provide GPUs with NVLink-locality. Expect +10–20ms overhead for network/VM layer versus hosted local.
   - reed-13b-8bit: supported but verify mem-constrained instances; we recommend a 48GB class for stable tail latency.

3) Security / audit docs:
   - SOC 2 + audit evidence pack: https://drive.redwood.ai/security/soc2_axn_evidence (read-only)
   - For the eval, we recommend minimal PII redaction and a signed evaluation MOU; procurement template available on the Drive link.

Rationale notes (short):
- We prioritized the 7b-fp16 model for the first sprint because it balances quality and latency for RAG/chat. The 13b-8bit is our pick for quality-critical flows (summaries/escalations) where you accept higher cost. The 1.3b-quant is explicitly for high-volume, cheap lookups and can act as a default fallback to keep unit economics down.

Operational asks for the ops call:
- Confirm a test dataset window (we suggest last 30 days of anonymized transcripts).
- Provide a VPN/IP allowlist for the Dedicated pilot (if you go that route).
- MOU / procurement contact to ingest initial pricing ask (we’ll draft a short commercial outline for the 1-month trial + 6-month commit).

I’ve attached a short latency profile we pulled from the overnight harness (latency_profile_7b.pdf) and updated the benchmarks CSV with per-sequence histograms.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
